summary: Frank E. Reynolds worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He spent his career at the University of Chicago, serving as Professor (~1967–2001) and later Emeritus (~2001–2019).

Frank Ernest Keay was an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his B.A. (~1897–1900) and M.A. (1917) from the University of London. He served as Principal of Talghari Boys’ School (1922) and priest at Bishop Cotton School (1941–1944).
Frank F. Conlon is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Minnesota (1969). He spent his academic career at the University of Washington as Professor Emeritus (~1969–2004).

Frank J. Hoffman works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, under doctoral supervisor Stewart Sutherland, and with Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, Prithwish Neogy, Rama Nath Sharma, and Kashi Nath Upadhyaya.

Frank J. Korom is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed graduate studies at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 1990) and served as Professor at Boston University (attested 2005).

Frank Lee Woodward studied at Christ's Hospital and Sidney Sussex College (B.A., M.A. ~1890–1902) under Caroline Rhys Davids. An Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, he taught at multiple schools, served as Dekan at Mahinda College (1903–1919), and translated for the Pali Text Society.

Frank Lillingston was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Pembroke College, earning a B.A. (~1891–1894) and M.A. (~1894–1898), and served as Theological Lecturer at Selwyn College (1897–1898).

Frank Raymond Allchin was an archaeologist and Indologist. He earned his BA and doctorate at the University of London under K. de B. Codrington, later holding posts at SOAS (1954–1959), Cambridge (1959–1989), and the Ancient India and Iran Trust (~1978–2010).

Frank Walter Nicolson was a scholar of Indology and classics who studied at Mount Allison University (B.A. ~1879–1883) and Harvard (A.B. ~1883–1887). He was an Instructor in Sanskrit at Harvard (1888–1889) and Professor of Latin at Wesleyan University (1913–1934).
Frank Whittingham Skemp studied linguistics and Indology. He received a B.A. from the University of Manchester (~1897–1900) and studied at Peterhouse (1903–1904) in preparation for the I.C.S.

Frank-Richard Hamm was an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Dr. phil. (1940–1948) and habilitation (~1952–1957) at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring. He held posts at Hamburg, the Free University of Berlin (1964), and Bonn (1965).

Franklin Edgerton, a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, earned his Ph.D. at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield (1906–1909). He served as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926), Yale University (1926–1953), and Banaras Hindu University (1953–1954).

Frans Wilhelm Gustaf Hjelt was an Indologist who earned an M.A. from the University of Helsinki (~1836–1840) and studied at Uppsala University under Otto Fredrik Tullberg (1842–1843). He held posts at Helsinki (1844) and Turun Katedraalikoulu (Rector, 1845–1872).
František Kamarýt was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University (~1913–1917), where he earned his Ph.D. under doctoral supervisor Josef Zubatý.

František Čupr was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his Ph.D. from Charles University (~1841–1845). He taught at Akademické gymnázium v Praze (1848–1853), was PD at Charles University (1849), and became principal of Prague First Private Czech Gymnasium (1853).

František Šohaj was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned a Ph.D. from Charles University (~1845–1848). He served as Professor of Philosophy at Charles University (1848–1859) and held a post at Akademické gymnázium v Praze (1859).

Franz Altheim was a historian and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Goethe University Frankfurt (1916–1921). He held positions at Frankfurt (PD 1928), Halle-Wittenberg (Professor 1936), and the Free University of Berlin (Professor ord. 1950–1965).

Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned a BA from UC Berkeley, an MA from the Graduate Theological Union, and a Ph.D. from the University of Chicago, later serving as Instructor at California State University, Los Angeles (1998).

Franz August Schmölders was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Bonn (~1832–1836) and studied in Paris. He held posts as PD at Berlin (1842) and Professor at the University of Breslau (1846).

Franz Bernhard was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt (1952–1960) and completed his habilitation at Frankfurt (-1965). He held posts at Frankfurt and as Prof. Dr. at the University of Hamburg (1966–1971).
